title: What sessions have spent, and what they said
description: GET /v1/orchestrator/usage and GET /v1/transcript. Both read the assistants' own records, so both carry evidence rather than presenting a number with no source.

model.description: Empty where the record did not name one. Codex's cumulative total does not, and it is left blank rather than guessed from the session's current configuration, which can have changed partway through a thread.

UsageRow.description: One session's usage, as its own transcript records it. This is what the transcript accounts for, which is a smaller claim than what the session spent: one conversation's own turns cannot see work another model did on its behalf.

messages.description: How many assistant turns were counted. Absent for a source that reports a cumulative total rather than per-turn figures.

note.description: Why a row could not be read. Present with `evidence: none`, and never alongside a number.

totalTokens.description: The sum of the rows that could be read. Rows carrying `evidence: none` contribute nothing, so this can be smaller than the truth and never larger.

TranscriptEntry.description: One thing in a conversation, in the shape the Swift app's `transcriptRows` writes it. A tool call and what the tool returned both carry `role: tool`; only the call names its tool. A call's `text` is the one line describing what it was asked to do — a command, a path, a query — which is what a folded row shows as its subject. An `AskUserQuestion` call carries its questions instead, after the U+0001 `ask` U+0001 marker.

artifacts.description: Pictures an assistant turn showed with a `<clawdline-image>` marker, or a Clawdline session message carried. Resolved against this daemon's store and then, read-only, the Swift app's.

at.description: Unix seconds. Absent when the record carried no timestamp this reader accepts.

fileChanges.description: Exact edits: a Codex patch, or the whole file a Claude `Write` created. Absent on every other entry.

imageCount.description: Images attached to a user turn. Absent when there were none: the Swift app writes an explicit 0 on user rows, and a reader treats absence as that 0.

role.description: user, assistant, peer (another Claude Code session), message (another session through Clawdline), notice (Clawdline about a task) or tool.

source.description: The human-facing name of the session a peer or message row came from.

sourceAssistant.description: Which assistant sent a Clawdline session message.

sourceMode.description: How a peer or message row arrived: the peer's own mode, or `clawdline`.

tool.description: The tool a call used. Absent on a tool's result and on prose.

content.description: The whole file, for an addition, a deletion or a Claude `Write`.

kind.description: add, delete, update or write, as the record spelled it; `change` when it did not.

status.description: pending, inProgress or completed — Codex app-server's spelling, not the rollout's in_progress.

TranscriptActivity.description: What a Codex tool item recorded about itself: `called` for an MCP call with a title, `explored` for a shell command Codex classified as reads and searches.

durationMs.description: How long the item took. -1 when the record did not say, which the Swift app sends as an absent key; 0 is a real, sub-millisecond duration and is drawn as one.

result.description: A called tool's result text, cut at 4,000 characters.

TranscriptNotice.description: A decoded Clawdline notice without its protocol, version and body — the Swift app's `webObject`. Which fields are present depends on `kind`: task_finished, workspace_overlap, file_wait_request, file_wait_release or handoff_receipt.

outstanding.description: task_finished only, where the decoder requires it, so absence there means 0.

TranscriptTruncation.description: The newest entries were kept and older ones left out, because the whole page would have passed its byte budget.

TranscriptPage.description: `entries`, `signature` and `truncation` are the Swift app's transcript payload; `evidence`, `path` and `note` say where the reading came from.

path.description: Which file this was read from. A reading that cannot name its source is not evidence.

signature.description: The record's size and modification time, `<bytes>-<unix seconds>`, and empty when nothing was read. It changes whenever the entries could have.
